input: Research Carvana (carvana.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: The next defined operating catalyst is Q4 2026: management expects retail units sold to increase sequentially and full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to land at the high end of its previously communicated $2.7-$3.0 billion range, assuming a stable environment; the fiscal quarter ends December 31, 2026.

Carvana’s investor-relations events page states that there are currently no upcoming events scheduled, so no separately dated earnings call, investor conference, product launch, court decision, index change, or lock-up expiry could be verified for the next six months.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026 reported October 28: 217,385 retail units (+39.4% year over year), $8.040 billion revenue (+42.4%), $483 million net income, and $800 million Adjusted EBITDA; EBITDA margin was 10.0%.
Against consensus, Q3 revenue of $8.040 billion beat the $7.838 billion estimate, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.39 missed the $0.4485 estimate by about 13%.
Current company guidance is qualitative for Q4 unit growth plus full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA at the high end of $2.7-$3.0 billion; the company did not provide quantitative revenue or EPS guidance.

The reported quarter was operationally strong but lower quality on per-unit economics: total gross profit per retail unit fell to $6,997 from $7,362 and Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3% year over year.

event_driven.claim: On August 14, 2026, Carvana entered a $1.66 billion senior secured Term Loan B maturing August 14, 2033; proceeds and cash on hand were used to redeem the $1.66 billion 2030 Senior Secured Notes in full.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Carvana acquired two franchise dealerships for $40 million total consideration ($19 million cash and $21 million trade vehicle floor-plan payables); the filing says the acquisitions were not material.
Q3 2026 other expense included derecognition of the original Root warrants as a result of a 2026 Warrant Exchange transaction; the cited filing section does not disclose a transaction value.

credit_signals.claim: As of September 30, 2026, total debt was $5.161 billion, including $2.269 billion of Senior Secured Notes, $1.660 billion of Term Loan B, $107 million of Senior Unsecured Notes, and $1.125 billion of asset-based financing; cash and cash equivalents were $3.049 billion.

Liquidity resources were reported at $7.503 billion, comprising $3.049 billion cash, $2.071 billion short-term revolving availability, $1.500 billion super-senior debt capacity, $750 million pari-passu senior debt capacity, and $133 million unpledged securitization interests.

Near-term debt dates include $32 million of 2027 Senior Unsecured Notes due April 15, 2027, a $1.5 billion Floor Plan Facility renewed through April 30, 2027, and finance-receivable revolvers maturing February 14, March 29, June 30, and October 15, 2027; the Term Loan B begins quarterly amortization in the quarter ending March 31, 2027.

The Term Loan B has no financial maintenance covenant but includes restrictions on additional debt, liens, restricted payments, asset sales, mergers and affiliate transactions; Fitch assigned the proposed facility a BB+ rating and RR2 recovery rating before the final facility was upsized to $1.66 billion.

alternative_signals.claim: Q3 average monthly unique visitors increased to 23.790 million from 19.636 million year over year, while website inventory increased to 87,370 units from 67,236.

Q3 SG&A compensation and benefits rose to $255 million from $209 million and advertising to $152 million from $102 million; management attributed the broader SG&A increase to higher unit volume, employee headcount, advertising, logistics, fuel, limited warranty and IT expenses.

Carvana’s distribution network spanned 316 metropolitan statistical areas and serviced over 80% of the U.S. population as of September 30, 2026, supporting the company’s scale and delivery-density thesis.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Recent open-market selling was broad: on November 2-4, 2026, CFO Mark Jenkins sold 63,750 shares for about $4.58 million, Chief Product Officer Daniel Gill sold 253,639 shares for about $18.13 million, and director Ira Platt sold 29,640 shares for about $2.25 million; several other Form 4s were tax-withholding or derivative exercises rather than open-market sales.
Director Michael Maroone made a notable open-market purchase of 25,000 Class A shares for about $1.54 million on July 31, 2026.

Fiscal.ai’s current insider-holder record shows Ernest C. Garcia II with 254.7 million shares (35.24% of shares outstanding) and CEO Ernest C. Garcia III with 36.4 million shares (5.03%), including direct and trust-held positions; the latest underlying holdings were filed November 1, 2026 for the CEO and October 30, 2026 for Garcia II.

risks.claim: The Q3 per-unit economics weakened: total gross profit per retail unit declined 5.0% year over year to $6,997 and Adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 10.0% from 11.3%, leaving the thesis dependent on continued volume growth and operating leverage.

Carvana identifies exposure to used-vehicle prices, benchmark interest rates, inflation, fuel and energy costs, tariffs and trade restrictions, competition, and geopolitical events; it said higher rates and inflation can reduce vehicle affordability and demand.

The company is party to legal and regulatory disputes, including putative class actions alleging federal securities-law, consumer-protection, labor/employment, and vehicle titling and registration violations.

Carvana says used-vehicle sales are seasonal, with the lowest relative level of vehicle sales generally expected in the fourth calendar quarter, while used vehicles generally depreciate faster in the fourth and first quarters.

The business remains exposed to securitization-market risk because it relies on selling originated finance receivables and retains beneficial interests subject to underlying credit and prepayment risk.

output.research_view: Carvana’s core long thesis is still volume and scale: Q3 set records for units, revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and digital traffic and inventory expanded. The near-term debate is quality of growth—Q3 non-GAAP EPS missed consensus and per-unit gross profit and EBITDA margin fell—while the refinancing extended major secured debt but leaves $5.2 billion of debt, financing-market exposure and 2027 maturities to monitor. With no confirmed upcoming IR event listed, Q4 execution against qualitative unit guidance and the high end of the EBITDA range is the key observable catalyst; recent executive selling is a meaningful sentiment counter-signal.
missing_fields: confirmed dated earnings or other corporate event after 2026-11-10
current post-October-2026 agency rating action beyond the Fitch term-loan rating
institutional 13F position changes and current 13D/13G activist positions
current hiring, layoff, contract-win/loss, pricing-change or trade-press channel-check evidence
